subject: SIG: deployment isolation + evidence request — hosted / dedicated / private
messages:

Subject: SIG: deployment isolation and evidence request (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)

Hi Rishi / Laura,

Thanks for taking this — Acme's security team is finishing our SIG for procurement and we need a concise explanation and artifacts that map how Redwood's three deployment modes differ with respect to: tenancy/isolation, customer data residency, key management options (customer-managed KMS/HSM), audit/logging access, SOC 2 scope, and supported network architectures (VPC peering, private endpoints, on-prem agents).

Specifically we need by EOD Thu, Jun 4: a one-page matrix that we can attach to the SIG, any SOC 2 scope statement that clarifies what is in/out for each mode, and a checklist for Private/VPC/on-prem packaging so our infra team can validate.

If you can also point to engineering evidence (design docs, runbook links, or a contact) for the Private/on-prem option that would be ideal. We may have follow-ups.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a short call if that helps.

Thanks,
Elena Cruz

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SIG: deployment isolation and evidence request (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask. I've attached a concise matrix and an initial SIG response doc that should cover the items you listed. High-level summary below (please see attached matrix for one-line guidance you can paste into the SIG):

- Hosted (Redwood API / multi-tenant):
  - Tenancy: logical multi-tenant separation on shared GPU pools; isolation via request scoping and strict tenant metadata separation.
  - Data residency: customer data may be processed in our hosted regions; we support region pinning for data locality.
  - Key management: Redwood-managed keys by default; we support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for specific enterprise plans via cloud KMS integrations.
  - Logging / audit: comprehensive request/response tracing, tenant-scoped audit logs retained per the SOC 2 retention policy; access controls for customer-specific log access requests.
  - SOC 2: Hosted endpoints are in-scope for Redwood's SOC 2 report (see attached statement).

- Dedicated (reserved capacity / single-tenant GPU pools):
  - Tenancy: dedicated GPU pools provisioned for a single customer — compute isolation is guaranteed at the pool level.
  - Data residency: strong region pinning and optional dedicated storage.
  - Key management: customer can elect customer-managed keys (KMS) for data-at-rest and select transit encryption.
  - Logging / audit: tenant-isolated telemetry and longer retention options; we can provide scoped audit exports.
  - SOC 2: Dedicated is covered by Redwood's SOC 2 when services are operated by Redwood; private network links / customer-managed control planes may carve out some components (see matrix).

- Private / VPC / On-prem:
  - Tenancy: customer-managed environment; Redwood provides an optional control plane agent or packaging but compute/control lives in customer VPC or on-prem.
  - Data residency: fully customer-controlled.
  - Key management: customer owns keys and HSM/KMS integrations; Redwood can integrate with customer HSMs where required.
  - Logging / audit: audit logs typically remain in the customer's logging stack; Redwood can ship agent hooks to forward or mirror events.
  - SOC 2: Private deployments are generally outside Redwood's hosted SOC 2 scope because critical infrastructure components are customer-managed — however, Redwood can provide evidence for components we operate and a clear boundary-of-scope statement.

I've attached: redwood_sig_deployment_matrix.pdf (one-page matrix), and a draft acme_sig_answers_v1.docx with suggested text for the SIG questionnaire. If you want a more formal SOC 2 carve-out statement for Private, I can loop Legal & Security to produce that doc.

If you'd like, we can run a 30-minute technical walkthrough with your infra team to go over the Private packaging.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

> Laura / Dev — forwarding Acme's request and the matrix I sent. Action items: 
>
> 1) Dev — can you confirm the exact wording for SOC 2 scope phrasing for Dedicated vs Private?
> 2) Dev — verify audit log retention windows for Dedicated (standard vs extended options) and whether we can export tenant-scoped logs on demand.
> 3) Laura — please review the acme_sig_answers_v1.docx; if Sales/legal want modifications before I send final, flag them.

Thanks — quick replies inline below.

1) SOC 2 scope phrasing (suggested single-sentence answers for the SIG):
- Dedicated: "Redwood's SOC 2 report covers the Redwood-managed control plane and compute services used to host Dedicated deployments; where Redwood operates the infrastructure the services are included in our SOC 2 scope. Customer-managed network appliances or customer-operated control planes are excluded."
- Private/VPC/On-prem: "Private deployments where the customer operates the control plane and compute are outside Redwood's SOC 2 scope; Redwood can provide evidence for components we deliver/manage (installation packages, agent binaries, and operational runbooks)."

2) Audit logs / retention / exports:
- Default retention (hosted/dedicated): 90 days for request-level telemetry and 365 days for aggregated audit trails (compliant with our SOC 2 policy).
- Extended retention: available as an add-on (custom agreements can extend to 3+ years).
- Export: tenant-scoped audit exports available for Dedicated and Hosted via secure S3 export or direct streaming to customer SIEM (on request). For Private, logs are routed to the customer's stack by default; agent hooks support streaming to customer endpoints.

3) Private deploy checklist: attached redwood_private_deploy_checklist.xlsx (includes network ports, agent install steps, HSM/KMS integration notes, minimal kernel module requirements for accelerated inference, and a pre-runbook checklist).

Notes / caveats to include in the SIG (recommend adding these as footnotes):
- Where we say "SOC 2 covers X" that assumes Redwood operates the control plane and provisioning services; any customer-managed replacement (control plane, key storage, networking) will change the boundary.
- For BYOK / HSM integrations, there may be additional onboarding lead time and an integration security review.

If this looks good I can mark the draft as engineering-reviewed and you can send the final to Acme.

Attachment: redwood_private_deploy_checklist.xlsx (xlsx stub)

—
